note: Which of our realms a Cliopatria polity is, where the rules of tools/history/borders/build.py decide wrongly. realm: a realm key of setup_1291.json; 'union' (the polity unites realms that keep their own titles; our division stays); 'new' (a realm of its own); or as: the same realm as another Cliopatria polity. A realm is the state: its name follows the polity (a name event), its holder follows the ruler list of its title.

French First Republic.why: the French state; the list of French monarchs has no holder 1792-1804

First French Empire.why: the French state; Napoleon I is in the list of French monarchs

Bourbon Kingdom of France.why: the French state; Louis XVIII in the list

French Second Republic.why: the French state; no holder from February 1848

Kingdom of Great Britain.why: Acts of Union 1707: England and Scotland as one state; England holds most of it

British Empire.why: the possessions of the British crown in the frame (Gibraltar, Malta, Ionian Islands)

Kingdom of Prussia.why: Brandenburg-Prussia, the same state, royal title from 1701

Duchy of Prussia.why: the secularised state of the Teutonic Order 1525, a duchy of its own until united with Brandenburg

Kingdom of Poland.why: the kingdom restored 1320 (Wladyslaw I), one title over Greater Poland and Krakow-Sandomierz

Kingdom of Spain.head: castile
Kingdom of Spain.why: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Spain is the whole composite monarchy (Castile, Aragon, Naples, Sicily; 1529-1555 even Charles V's Austrian lands): each crown keeps its title; Castile is its head

Spanish Empire.why: the crowns of Castile, Aragon, Naples, Sicily under one king, each its own title
Spanish Empire.head: castile

Habsburg Monarchy.why: the lands of the Habsburgs: Austria, Bohemia, Hungary keep their titles
Habsburg Monarchy.head: austria

Austrian Empire.why: 1804: still Austria, Bohemia, Hungary each its title
Austrian Empire.head: austria

Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.why: Crown of Poland and Grand Duchy of Lithuania, two titles
Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.head: c_kingdom_of_poland

Holy Roman Empire.why: the Empire is no state of its own here: its members keep their lands

Holy Roman Empire Minor States.why: Cliopatria's lump of the small estates of the Empire

Duchies of Poland.why: the Piast duchies, each its own

Kalmar Union.why: Denmark, Norway, Sweden under one crown, three titles
Kalmar Union.head: denmark

Iberian Union.why: Portugal and Spain under one king 1580-1640, separate titles
Iberian Union.head: castile

Electorate of Hanover.why: Brunswick-Lüneburg, elector from 1692; in personal union with Great Britain, not part of it

Bessarabia.why: 1812 Treaty of Bucharest: eastern Moldavia became the Bessarabia Governorate of the Russian Empire

Ottoman Tripolitania.why: 1835: the Ottomans ended the Karamanli dynasty and ruled Tripoli directly as a province

Beylik of Tunis.why: the beys of Tunis (Muradids, Husainids) under Ottoman suzerainty, not the Hafsid title that ended 1574; same name only

Cisalpine Republic.why: 1797: a French sister republic in Lombardy and Emilia, a new state (not a union of the old ones)

Kingdom of Etruria.why: 1801: the Grand Duchy of Tuscany made a kingdom for the House of Bourbon-Parma by France, a new state

moscow.title: Tsardom of Russia
moscow.why: the list of grand princes ends 1547 because Ivan IV took the title of tsar; the state went on (Tsardom of Russia, Russian Empire 1721)

england.title: Kingdom of Great Britain
england.why: Acts of Union 1707: the English crown went on as the crown of Great Britain (United Kingdom 1801)

castile.title: Kingdom of Spain
castile.why: the Nueva Planta decrees dissolved the Crown of Castile into the Kingdom of Spain under the same king, Philip V

naples.title: Kingdom of the Two Sicilies
naples.why: 8 December 1816 Naples and Sicily became the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies under the same king, Ferdinand I

brunswick_lueneburg.title: Electorate of Hanover
brunswick_lueneburg.why: 1705 the principality of Lüneburg went by inheritance to the Electorate of Brunswick-Lüneburg (Hanover; Kingdom of Hanover 1814)

brandenburg.title: Kingdom of Prussia
brandenburg.why: the electorate ended with the Empire on 6 August 1806; its holder went on as King of Prussia

note_successions: A realm whose title ended while its state went on under another title of the same holder: the realm keeps its land and counts as held from that year (its holders under the new title are still to be added to the ruler lists).

aragon.why: Nueva Planta decree of 29 June 1707 abolished the Crown of Aragon; the list of Aragonese monarchs ends 1707

scotland.why: Acts of Union, in force 1 May 1707: Scotland and England became Great Britain

note_unions: head: the realm a union's conquests go to (the realm of its leading crown); league: a union without a holder of its own (the Empire, confederations, dynasties).
